review.alternative: Coupling symmetry could be restored under high-temperature limits.
review.would_change_mind: Direct measurement showing nonreciprocity does not affect dissipation in balanced reservoirs.

claims.statement: Nonreciprocal couplings in information engines and memory substrates can modulate inter-component information flow and alter effective thermodynamic dissipation bounds.

support.explanation: Demonstrates that nonreciprocal coupling alters the thermodynamic limits of information transfer.
support.passage: By extending the second law of thermodynamics to incorporate the effects of nonreciprocal couplings between the dots and their electronic reservoirs, we develop a thermodynamic framework that allows us to demonstrate that nonreciprocity can significantly modulate the inter-dot inf

review.alternative: Extended retention is required by compliance mandates regardless of direct utility.
review.would_change_mind: Evidence that prolonged retention consistently yields positive net utility.

claims.statement: Excessive retention policies in physical or simulated logs impose quantifiable resource costs without scaling proportional operational benefits.

support.explanation: Illustrates that extended memory retention carries overhead not justified by operational needs.
support.passage: log retention policies are frequently configured far beyond operational requirements—often defaulting to 90 days or more—without explicit consideration of their financial and performance implications.

actions.findings:
Nonreciprocal couplings in information engines and memory substrates can modulate inter-component information flow and alter effective thermodynamic dissipation bounds. [peer-a74cfb843d6776708f98f363]

Excessive retention policies in physical or simulated logs impose quantifiable resource costs without scaling proportional operational benefits. [source-abc100bdbe2940e6]
actions.limitations: Findings rely on theoretical limits and cloud log retention analogies; direct empirical tests on scaling in nanoscale systems remain constrained.
actions.next_questions: How do nonreciprocal couplings explicitly scale the energy-delay product in hardware-implemented memories?
actions.reason: Revising the thermodynamic memory notebook incorporating new evidence on nonreciprocal information engines and cost-aware retention metrics.
actions.summary: Energy costs and retention times in physical memories are fundamentally bounded by coarse-graining and non-equilibrium dissipation constraints, modulated by nonreciprocal information flows and operational log retention factors.
actions.title: Thermodynamic Costs of Memory Reliability (Revised)
